findings.title: Returned SQL fragments contain un-parenthesized top-level OR, enabling authorization bypass when callers append conditions
findings.body: `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` verbatim when there are no filters (line 75), and `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` are public. For org and team scope, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`/`buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` produce a fragment whose top-level operator is `OR` (e.g. `("teamId" = ANY($1)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true) OR (("userId" = ANY($2)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))` after the reduce), and `buildFilterConditions` likewise returns a bare `OR` fragment when only `eventTypeId` is set. Since the service no longer executes any query, every consumer must interpolate these fragments into their own raw SQL, and the natural `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" > ${x}` becomes `A OR (B AND x)` because SQL `AND` binds tighter than `OR`. That silently widens the authorized row set (bookings of users/teams the caller is not entitled to see). The service should wrap its final result in parentheses (e.g. `Prisma.sql`(${combined})`) before returning it from `getBaseConditions`/`getFilterConditions`/`getAuthorizationConditions`.

findings.title: Public `findMany` removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions` without updating consumers
findings.body: The only query-executing method on `InsightsBookingService` (`findMany(findManyArgs)`) is deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`. Nothing else in the repository is updated in this PR, so any existing caller of `service.findMany(...)` will fail to compile (or, if typed loosely, fail at runtime). It also pushes raw-SQL assembly onto every consumer, which is where the parenthesization hazard above becomes dangerous. Either keep an execution helper on the service (e.g. a `findMany`/`query` that wraps `$queryRaw` with the base conditions correctly parenthesized) or update all call sites in the same change.

findings.title: Constructor option type widened so `scope: "team"` without `teamId` type-checks and silently returns no rows
findings.body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`) instead of the zod-inferred discriminated union. A caller passing `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` with `teamId` undefined (a very likely shape when `teamId` comes from an optional request field) now compiles, but `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.safeParse` fails, `this.options` becomes `null`, and `buildAuthorizationConditions` returns `1=0`. The user sees an empty insights result with no error and no log, instead of a compile-time error as before. Keep the exact union type for the public options, or surface the validation failure (throw / log) rather than degrading to an empty result set.

findings.title: Only the user-scope SQL is ever executed; team/org `= ANY(...)` fragments are never run against Postgres
findings.body: After this conversion the correctness of the generated SQL (column quoting, `= ANY($n)` parameter binding for integer arrays, `1=0`) can only be verified by executing it. The single `$queryRaw` test at line 481 exercises the user-scope condition plus an `eventTypeId` filter; the team-scope, org-scope and NOTHING conditions are asserted only by comparing `Prisma.sql` template objects, which would pass even if the SQL is syntactically invalid or the driver cannot infer the array parameter type for `= ANY($1)`. Add `$queryRaw` assertions for at least the org and team scopes (and the NOTHING condition) so a broken raw query is caught by CI rather than in production.

findings.title: Caching tests for auth/filter conditions were deleted with no replacement
findings.body: The `describe("Caching")` block covering `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` memoization was removed. That behaviour still exists in the service (`cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` with the `=== undefined` sentinel check, which is specifically needed because `getFilterConditions()` legitimately caches `null`). With the tests gone, a regression such as switching the check to `if (!this.cachedFilterConditions)` — which would recompute and re-query on every call — would go unnoticed. Port the caching assertions to the new SQL expectations instead of dropping them.
